_comment: CIP identity -> catalog number mapping, mined directly from a locally-installed Rockwell Logix Designer / RSLogix 5000 copy's own module catalog data (not reverse-engineered from customer L5X files). Two source trees were merged: the modern per-catalog-number AOP profile XML under 'RSLogix 5000\Module Profiles\**\*.xml' (one file per catalog number, current for Studio 5000 v21+), and the legacy monolithic per-family 'Classic' catalog under 'RSLogix 5000\ENU\v20\Bin\*.xml' (kept by the installer for opening pre-v21 projects; covers some older/controller identities the modern tree no longer lists separately). Keys are 'vendor:product_type:product_code' (base catalog number, no series letter -- used when the module's firmware major revision is not known) or 'vendor:product_type:product_code:major_rev' (catalog number WITH series letter, e.g. '5069-OB16/B' -- used when the caller passes major_rev= to catalog_number_for_identity(), which ModuleBuilder does with the Major byte it already parses from the ACD binary's extended module record). The vendor/type/code triple alone does not encode the hardware series letter -- Rockwell ties the series to a per-catalog-family firmware-major-revision breakpoint instead, which is exactly what the *:major_rev entries capture verbatim from Rockwell's own data.
